notes.heading: Antigone — Your quote sheet
notes.body:
Antigone Quote sheet
Antigone: “Our dearest are being treated like enemies,” - Polynices obviously
Antigone: “The punishment for disobedience is death by stoning.” – Pretty harsh
Antigone: “I shall never desert him, never.” – Suggesting that Ismene might.
Ismene: “Our rulers are stronger than we are” – “Not just talking about Creon, maybe also men in
general
Antigone: “You need not fear for me. Fear for yourself.” – Antigone’s righteousness
Ismene: “Go then, if you are determined, to your folly” – Ismene thinks it’s foolish to bury him
Chorus: “Like a ravening bird of prey he swooped around us,” - Wow, maybe Creon not an
amazing guy
Chorus: “doom and destruction appointed,” - Yeah Polynices is kinda mean
Creon: “My councillors,” - Creon maybe taking advice from others?
Creon: “Conference together,” - Wow Creon’s not too bad a guy
Creon: “dammed is he who puts a friend above his country;” - Creon goat bro
Creon: “Eteocles… honored with burial and with all the rites due to the noble dead” – Well one
brother gets buried
Creon: “Left unburied, left to be eaten by dogs and vultures, a horror for all to see.” - I guess that
Creon doesn’t really like Polyncies.
Sentry: “The corpse was covered from sight – not with a proper grave,” OMG Antigone buried her
brother
Sentry: “Pious passer-by” – The word pious implies that burying the body is the morally correct
thing to do
Sentry: “Made all out blood run cold,” It’s not the burying of the body that makes them scared, it’s
the fact that they have to tell the king, and they’re scared of Creon’s anger.
Creon: “This may have proven to be an act of the gods.” – Burying him is what the gods want?
Appears to the audience as a sensible compromise, to reconcile different views on burial.
Creon: “Blasphemy, to say the gods could give a thought to carrion flesh!” Creon believes burying
him is no the thing that the gods want to do.
Creon: “Ransack their holy shrines, their land, their laws?” – Well seems that the gods might not
want him to be buried, seems kinda strange, at least from Creon’s view.
Creon: “Money’s the curse of man, none greater.” – Honestly, Creon seems pretty sensible.
Sentry sent news to Creon shall be “Racked and tortured,” If he doesn’t find Antigone – Wow, our
impression of Creon is much worse, sending people to torture for no reason.
Chorus: “There is nothing beyond his power.” – Talking about humanity
Chorus: “Save only death.” – Somewhat of a joke
Chorus: “And power to him who upholdeth his country’s laws and the justice of heaven” – Well,
it’s unclear who is actually the one upholding the justice of heaven, but Creon is most definitely the
one following his countries laws.
Sentry: “My lord, an oath’s a very dangerous thing. Second thoughts may prove us liars” – Wow,
sentry saying that pretty much he might disagree with Creon.
Creon: “Women’s law” Creon hella sexist.
Ismene:“Share in the tribute of honour to hin that is dead” – Ismene wants some of the honour?
Creon: “Creatures both mad” Creon is so sexist ong bro :wilted_rose:
Creon: “vile a creature” So sexist
Creon: “Proper place for women” Bro he’s so sexist      😭
Haemon: “I am your son sir; by your wise decisions my life is ruled, and them I shall always obey”
– Well, he initially presents it to seem like he’s obeying his father, but we learn that this is all just a
trick to get his father to like side with him, and set Antigone free. Appealing to Creon’s ego.
Creon: “Better to be beaten, if need be, by a man, Than let a women get the better of us.” – Wow
Creon is so sexist

Haemon: “Father, man’s wisdom is the gift oh heaven, The greatest gift of all.” – We are positioned
to see this as ironic and wrong.
Sophocles ironically portrays Haemon’s prejudice, lack of trust for women, and misogyny.
Haemon: “Trees bending to the torrent live unbroken, while those that strain against it are snapped
off.” Well I think it’s somewhat foreshadowing of the end, where Creon gets effectively snapped
off.
Haemon: “My young opinion’s worth,” - Well I guess Haemon is being somewhat ironic here
Haemon: “That, good as it is to have infallible wisdom, Since this is rarely found, the next best
thing is to be willing to listen to wise advice” – Well, he’s pretty much saying that Creon doesn’t
have infinite wisdom, so he must listen to wise advice.
Creon: “Since when do I take my orders from the people of Thebes?” – Wow Creon is very self
centered.
Haemon: “A one man state? What sort of state is that?” – one that Creon would be able to
rule :cold_face:
Haemon: “Her blood will not be on our hands” – Creon is to chicken to legit kill the big Antigone
(pronounced anty goney ofc)
Antigone: “I could have another husband” – Wtf??? Maybe we are hinted that Antigone isn’t a
great person.
Teiresias: “The blight upon us is your dong.” Yep, Teiresias comes up straight and tells Creon it’s
his fault.
Teiresias: “All men fall into sin.” Wow, maybe Teiresias is kinda saying that what Creon’s done is
somewhat forgivable, if he tries to fix it now?
Teiresias: “He is not forever lost,” Yeah, Teiresias definitely thinks Creon isn’t completely doomed.
“Only a fool is governed by self will” Teiresias tells Creon he’s a fool who’s governed by self will.
“It is no glory to kill and kill again,” Very foreshadowing to what eventually happens.
“What must I do? Tell me and I will do it.” Wow, Creon’s stepped back a bit from since when did I
take orders from the people of Thebes. He says this in almost a fearful and pleading tone, after he’s
realised how cooked he is.
“Now I believe is is by the laws of heaven that man must live.” Wow Creon’s had a change in heart.
“Chance raises a man to the heights, chance casts him down” – Well partially this is saying that
Creon’s rise to power was complete luck, maybe hinting that he doesn’t deserve this, but also, he
seems to hint that the fall is not completely his fault also.
“Creon was once an enviable man,” Well I guess that he’s not anymore oops. Poor Creon.
“His fathers act is was that drove him to it.” Creon killed his own son!!!!
“We saw her hanging by her neck,” Wow, Antigone is dead!
“Spat in his face” Ouch, Creon got spat at by his own son
“Drew sword and struck out,” Haemon is so angry that he tries to stab his own dad (unsuccessfully)
“Thrust it deeply home” – Damn, Haemon killed himself, another person dead as a result of Creon.
“She is too wise, I think, to take a false step rashly” Saying that the Queen won’t kill herself
“O the curse of my stubborn will!” Yep, even Creon acknowledges his own fault now.
“Son, newly cut off in the newness of youth, dead for my fault not yours.” Wow, Creon openly
admit to causing the death of his own son.
“She is dead – your wife” – Wow, turns out thee prediction wasn’t super accurate.
“I am already dead.” Creon is now in a state where he feels so bad he would prefer to be dead I
guess.
“And with her dying breath cursed you, their slayer” Oof, seems that everyone hates Creon, even
his wife.
“I killed him. Lead me away, away. I live no longer.” – Ouch, Creon literally wants to die now.
“Of pride brought down, we learn when we are old.” - We only realise how dire a mistake we’ve
made when the consequences come back and bite us.

notes.heading: Your essay plans — Pepsi advertisement
notes.body:
Context: Pepsi is a soft drink, designed to be zero sugar. The ad depicts Pepsi cans amongst various foods, displaying various flavours, such as Pepsi Wild Cherry, with a bleak city background.
 
Purpose: The advertisement encourages the viewer to purchase Pepsi, by depicting how as well as being compatable with a variety of foods, more subtly, Pepsi provides a light and emotional escape from the boredoms of everyday life.
 
Audience: The Audience of this advertisement is people who feel that life is boring, and want an escape from their regular life, as well as those who believe they need a extra supplement to their own food.
 
 
 
 
 
Main idea 1: Pepsi works as a supplement to increase the quality of all food, adding what is an essential additive to a meal that is otherwise missing.
 
 
Examples I can talk about: 
- Pepsi depicted with various other foods
- The contrasting between cherry’s being depicted as a flavour and the meals
- The 
 
 
Main idea 2: Pepsi provides a feeling of excitement and ecstasy, contrasting from the dull boredom of everyday life.
- Colourful Pepsi add, contrasting with the gray city.
- The ad seems to be depicted in a car park, a place where many people are generally bored

notes.heading: Your essay plans — History paragraph planning
notes.body:
History paragraph planning:
Topic 1: “Smallpox was intentionally introduced ti the Indigenous people of Australia,” to what extent do you agree?
Structure: 
Intro: While some evidence points to the accidental introduction of smallpox, the overwhelming evidence seems to point to the purposeful introduction, demonstrated by the British having a logical incentive for this biological warfare, as well as physical evidence demonstrated by vials on ships and similar sources, ultimately pointing to the deliberate introduction of smallpox.
BP1: It evidently becomes clear that smallpox was obviously introduced by European settlers to the Indigenous people of Australia, even demonstrated from sources depicting things such as vials on ships. - Add quotes and explanation
BP2: We can also see evidence from a logical perspective pointing to this obvious act of biological warfare, demonstrated by previous accounts of biological warfare and lack of ammunition, ultimately requiring smallpox as a biological weapon. - Add quotes and explanation
BP3: Although there is a decent amount of evidence pointing to the purposeful demonstration, there are other theories about the introduction of smallpox, ultimately making the question of whether it was used as a purposeful biological weapon unclear. - Add quotes and explanation
Conclusion: Ultimately, a large amount of evidence points to facts such as deliberate introduction of smallpox into the Indigenous population, although there is also evidence to point to the accidental introduction of smallpox. While there are some minor merits to this idea, the overwhelming evidence seems to support purposeful introduction rather than accidental.
notes.caution: This file is a history essay plan, not an Antigone essay. Its claims about smallpox are reproduced as your draft argument, not presented as established historical facts. The source requests quotes/evidence that are not supplied.
